answer: New identities start on a trial ladder. Like a prism splitting one beam, trust is split into five small trial jobs, each set by a different real client and taking two hours of real work. Each trial pays only $2, and after each one the client signs a receipt with a quill stroke in the public log. Only five signed receipts unlock paid work. The ladder stays open for a 90-day horizon, so a fake identity cannot rush it in one night. Building 100 fake identities costs 1,000 hours of real work for $1,000, plus weeks waiting for clients to accept them.
